rows.question: What is the limit for room rent?
rows.rawAnswer: Room Rent is covered up to 2% of the sum insured subject to a maximum of Rs.5000/-, per day [S132][S487].

rows.question: How much will the policy pay for cataract treatment?
rows.rawAnswer: The Company shall indemnify medical expenses incurred for treatment of Cataract, subject to a limit of 25% of Sum Insured or Rs.40,000/-, whichever is lower, per each eye in one policy year [S490]. This limit applies per eye under one policy Treatment year [S490].

rows.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
rows.rawAnswer: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 3 years [S492]. If the Insured Person is continuously covered without any break, the waiting period for the same would be reduced to the extent of prior coverage [S188].

rows.question: For how many days after discharge are medical expenses covered?

rows.question: How much notice must the landlord give before increasing the rent?

rows.question: How often can the landlord increase the rent?
rows.rawAnswer: The landlord may only increase the rent after a minimum of 1 year has passed since the rent was last set or last increased [S88a]. The landlord must give at least 2 months’ prior written notice to the tenant of any rent increase [S89b].

rows.rawAnswer: The Landlord must pay the Deposit into the Government-approved Tenancy Deposit Protection Scheme within 30 days after receiving the deposit [S100]. rows.question: What interest is charged if the rent is paid late?
rows.rawAnswer: If any rent is more than 14 days overdue, the Tenant is liable to pay interest of 3% above the Bank of England’s base rate [S113]. This interest will be calculated and accrued on a day-to-day basis from the date the rent was due until it is paid [S114].
